### 1. Request, authorisation, simulator behaviour
- Caller: Ingrid Solberg, managing member of Solberg Grain & Cattle LLC. She asks to "pay down the line by whatever it takes to get back within our borrowing base, today, out of the company's operating checking account". She leaves the figure to the representative and says she "will make the payment yourself once you are told the amount".
- Identification: phone 3084610372 → `find_customers` returns customer 5ed5b779-…, `member_number 'CPF-1520638'`, `tax_id_last4 '2417'`. When asked, the simulator gives CPF-1520638 and 2417. `verify_member_identity(customer_id, phone_number=3084610372, member_number=CPF-1520638, tax_id_last4=2417)` (at least 2 must match) comes before any account read.
- The simulator is passive. It waits while "something on the association's side has to be booked or worked out", it accepts a fee without asking for a waiver, and it runs the handed-over paydown exactly as given. That matches the KB: "This is the member's own tool. The servicing representative unlocks `authorize_shortfall_paydown_62bf68fd` and hands it over; the customer themselves runs it".

### 2. Act now, wait or refuse
Act now. Visible grounds:
- The line is `status 'active'`. The KB says "A payment may be applied only while the line is in active, suspended or matured status", and a certificate may be accepted/recorded "for a line in active or suspended status".
- Cure window. The paydown rule says it "is made within the product's deficiency cure period, in calendar days, after the certificate's received date, that date being day 0". For the Borrowing Base Operating Line the cure period is 10 days (reporting covenant schedule). The latest certificate was received 2026-09-17 (day 0), so the window runs through 2026-09-27. Today, 2026-09-21, is day 4, which is inside it.
- Two association-side writes must come first (item 6). They are within the agent's own power, so this is not a wait on any future condition.

### 4. Scored parameters
**(a) The association's borrowing base on certificate fce73d52.** Source: "Collateral Examination Worksheet" (the baseline: the six classes × the product rates, added together and rounded once). Factor documents found from the records:
- Stored grain rate. "Stored Grain Advance Rate for Members Financing Grain Storage…": "plus 5 points when the member holds a Grain Storage & Handling Loan in active status whose pledged collateral value is at least USD 250,000". The equipment record `Grain Storage & Handling Loan`, active, collateral_value 380,000 puts the rate at 80%.
- Late receipt. "Collateral Policy on Late-Received Certificates": received 17 days after the as-of date is ">15 but no more than 30", so grain and livestock are taken at 0.9.
- Prepaid inputs. "Advance Rate on Prepaid Crop Inputs as the Term Runs": term start 2026-03-01 (last renewal), as-of 2026-08-31 = 5 whole months, which falls in "at least 3 but fewer than 6", so 0.5 × 70 = 35%.
- Receivables. "Receivables Advance Rate … Certificate Reporting Record": 9 certificates have an as-of date within the twelve whole months before 2026-09-21 (the one being figured included). That is "at least 6 but fewer than 11", so 70%.
- Insured growing crop rate. "Advance Rate on Insured Growing Crops by Coverage Level": the crop-year assigned policy has 80% coverage, which is "at least 80 percent", so 70%.
- Insured growing crop value. "Insured Growing Crop Values Counted": the harvest price has not been released, so the value is the lower of the stated 640,000 and the guarantee at the projected price, 198 × 820 × 80% × 4.62 = 600,082.56.

Arithmetic:
- grain 300,000 × 0.9 × 80% = 216,000
- contracted 210,000 × 85% = 178,500
- livestock 240,000 × 0.9 × 75% = 162,000
- receivables 110,000 × 70% = 77,000
- prepaid 100,000 × 35% = 35,000
- crops 600,082.56 × 70% = 420,057.792
- Total 1,088,557.792 → **1,088,557.79**.

Fall-back (worksheet plus rate schedule only, with the policy qualifying at the 65% product rate): 225,000 + 178,500 + 180,000 + 88,000 + 70,000 + 416,000 = **1,157,500.00**. This is definite and different.

**(b) Overadvance fee on advance aba8318d.** Baseline from "Pricing the Overadvance Portion":
- Lending limit = min(1,600,000; 1,088,557.79) = 1,088,557.79.
- Principal from history = advances 1,895,000 − principal payments 740,000 = 1,155,000. Before the advance it was 1,060,000.
- Available credit immediately before = 28,557.79. Overadvance portion = 66,442.21 (within the 5% tolerance of 80,000).
- Baseline fee = 66,442.21 × 1.00% = 664.42 (fall-back).

Factors found from the records:
- History. "Repeat Overadvance Pricing": one overadvance fee (2025-11-06, 546.33) in the twelve whole months before today, so 1.5%.
- Channel. "Request Channel and Proceeds Delivery Points": channel `online_banking`, so +0.25.
- Depth. "Deep Use of the Tolerance": 66,442.21 / 80,000 = 0.83, which is at least 0.75, so +0.5.
- Farmland relief. "Farm Real Estate Relationship Relief": an active FRE loan on automatic payment, so × 0.75.
- Technical overadvance. "Technical Overadvances Drawn Before a New Certificate Is Verified": the advance came 1 day after the certificate was received (2026-09-17), so × 0.5.

Fee = 66,442.21 × 2.25% × 0.75 × 0.5 = 560.606146875 → **560.61**, rounded once. It is booked against source_txn_id aba8318d. The fee is dated today, the day "the borrowing base that reveals it is recorded".

**(c) Shortfall paydown.** Baseline from "Shortfall Paydown Amount": principal − lendable limit = 1,155,000 − 1,088,557.79 = 66,442.21. This is the fall-back once (a) is recorded. If the member's own figure 1,214,300 were used, the result would be 0. Factors:
- Reserve. "Unpaid Interest and Fee Reserve": billed interest unpaid = 0 (every bill paid; the latest, due 2026-09-10, was paid 2026-09-09). Fees not yet paid or waived = the new overadvance fee 560.61, since all earlier fees were paid or waived. So the reserve is "the unpaid fees alone", 560.61, and the limit after the reserve is 1,087,997.18.
- Cushion. "Lendable Limit Cushion After Recent Overadvance Fees": two overadvance fees "in the twelve whole months before today" (2025-11-06 and today's 560.61), so 0.98 × 1,087,997.18 = 1,066,237.2364.
- Shortfall = 1,155,000 − 1,066,237.2364 = 88,762.7636.
- Land equity. "Land-Equity Allowance": land equity 2,450,000 − 1,310,000 = 1,140,000, which is at least 0.5 × 1,600,000, so 1.0% × 1,600,000 = 16,000.
- Indemnity. "Assigned Crop Insurance Indemnity Credit": 18,400 determined and not paid, less 2,150 premium owed = 16,250.
- Paydown = 88,762.7636 − 16,000 − 16,250 = 56,512.7636 → **56,512.76**.

Residual visible-surface uncertainty, recorded honestly: the corpus never says outright whether a fee dated today falls "in the twelve whole months before today". If today's fee is not counted, the cushion tier is "exactly one" (limit − 5,000 = 1,082,997.18) and the paydown is **39,752.82**. I chose the inclusive reading for two reasons. The corpus uses "within one whole month before today" for a payment "returned last week", i.e. a period running up to the present. And the paydown's own prerequisite makes the paydown wait on the fee "standing".

2. find_operating_lines / find_operating_borrowing_base / find_operating_transactions. Also find_equipment_loans, find_cropins_policies, find_cropins_transactions, find_farmland_loans.

4. (agent) unlock + call `assess_overadvance_fee_10e059b9`(line_id 8bb5e857-…, source_txn_id aba8318d-…, amount 560.61).
5. (agent) `unlock_user_discoverable_tool('authorize_shortfall_paydown_62bf68fd')` and tell the member line_id 8bb5e857-… and amount 56512.76. (user) The member calls it, and the receipt shows status "applied".

Terminal state: the certificate carries 1,088,557.79, one new overadvance fee of 560.61 points to aba8318d, and one phone principal payment of 56,512.76 brings principal to 1,098,487.24.

### 6. Problem tree derived from visible materials alone
- Root P0, shortfall paydown (the customer's own write). Its hub "Borrowing Base Shortfall Paydowns on Operating Lines of Credit" states two prerequisite sentences:
  - S1: "The shortfall paydown is not fixed until the association has worked out its own borrowing base for the line's most recent certificate and recorded it in place of the member's own figure."
  - S2: "The shortfall paydown is fixed only after an overadvance fee stands against the line's latest advance whenever that advance took the line past its available credit."
- Hop P0 ← P1 (record the association's borrowing base). **State-derived.**
  - S1 names a state: the association's own borrowing base recorded on the most recent certificate.
  - Searching "association's own borrowing base" / "recorded" finds "The Association's Own Borrowing Base on a Delivered Certificate". It says "records it on that certificate in place of any figure the member worked out … The recording is due whenever a delivered certificate still carries a figure the association has not worked out itself."
  - Records: fce73d52 carries 1,214,300.00, but working it out under the association's worksheet and factor documents gives 1,088,557.79. So the certificate does not carry the association's figure, and the state does not hold.
- Hop P0 ← P2 (overadvance fee on the latest advance). **State-derived.**
  - S2 names a state: an overadvance fee standing against the latest advance, when that advance took the line past available credit.
  - Searching "overadvance fee" finds "Overadvance Fee Charges on Operating Lines of Credit": "charged once against an advance that took outstanding principal past the line's available credit, as a separate fee charge with the overadvance fee code pointing to that advance … the day that borrowing base is recorded".
  - Records: no `operating_fee_assessed` with fee_code overadvance points to aba8318d. Under the recorded borrowing base, the available credit before the advance was 28,557.79 < 95,000, so the condition is met and the state does not hold.
- Hop P2 ← P1. **State-derived.** The overadvance-fee hub states "The overadvance fee on the line's latest advance is fixed only after the association has recorded its own borrowing base on the line's most recent certificate." The records give the same order independently: with the member's 1,214,300 the advance would not exceed available credit at all.
- Dependency direction and order: P1 → P2 → P0. P1 and P2 are agent writes; P0 is the member's write.
- No hop was pre-solved. No document gave me another problem's tool name, route or chain. Each depended-on document was reached through the words the sentence and the records use ("association's own borrowing base", "overadvance fee", "fee code", "certificate").

### Two-way counter-proof
- "Do only the paydown": using the certificate as it stands (1,214,300) gives principal 1,155,000 below the limit, so a zero paydown. Equally it could be read as "nothing to pay". This is excluded by S1, and by the recording document's rule that the certificate's borrowing base is "the association's own figure, not the member's" ("On the Operating Lines of Credit, the borrowing base that stands on a borrowing base certificate is the association's own figure"). Paying down after recording but without the fee is excluded by S2. It would also leave the reserve and cushion understated (reserve 0 instead of 560.61; cushion tier "exactly one").
- Closest alternative object: an older certificate. Excluded by "the line's certificate with the latest as-of date" (paydown amount doc and worksheet).
- Alternative time anchor for the cure window: as-of date versus received date. The retired clause used the "submitted date"; the in-force paydown rule says "after the certificate's received date". Either way today is within 10 days of 2026-09-17.
- Alternative fee base: the product rate alone, or channel points omitted. Excluded by the factor ladders above, each reached from the record field (fee code history, `channel`, FRE autopay, certificate received date).
- Alternative paydown source or channel: the tool books "one principal payment received by phone". The simulator names Hastings checking 5531, but the tool takes no account parameter, so nothing more is needed.
- Calculation fall-backs, written down: borrowing base 1,157,500.00; fee 664.42; paydown 66,442.21 (or 0 on the member's figure). All three are definite and differ from the answers.
- Factor findability: every factor was reached from the words of a record. `Grain Storage & Handling Loan` led to the stored-grain rate doc. Certificate `submitted_date` versus `as_of_date` led to the late-receipt doc. Crop Insurance `Revenue Protection 80% Coverage`, `harvest_price ''` and `assigned_loan_id` led to the two growing-crop docs and the indemnity credit. `last_renewed_date` led to the prepaid doc. The certificate count led to receivables. `fee_code 'overadvance'` in the history led to the history and cushion docs. `channel 'online_banking'` led to the channel doc. FarmLand `autopay_enrolled True` and the collateral/principal fields led to the relief and land-equity docs. Billed interest and fee entries led to the reserve. No computation document hinted that a variation exists.

Two-way checks against the source:
- Window boundary. The source counts with `COUNT(within_months=12)`. Per the check_compute DSL, that means rows with 0 ≤ whole months to today < 12, today included. The effect field of the shortfall←overadvance-fee edge says the fee "joins the count … that sets the cushion". So the inclusive reading I chose blind is the source's reading.
- Visible weak point (not a KB defect). Neither the source's rule prose nor the KB states in words that a row dated today falls "in the twelve whole months before today". The KB carries the source sentence verbatim. A careful reader settles it from the prerequisite sentence, as I did blind. This is recorded as a policy-side note, because the source prose leaves the boundary unstated and only its compute closes it.
- No hidden compute, GT or raw initial_state was needed to reach any value.
- No visible sentence supports a different action, object, order or terminal state.

Out-of-scope note (for the coordinator, not a KB verdict): the GT verify_member_identity omits phone_number. The agent system prompt says to pass "exactly the identifying values the caller gives". Whether a rollout that also passes the phone given at lookup is scored as matching belongs to the policy/scoring layer.

**Verdict: KB-RUNTIME PASS** (task 0).
